correctness.rationale: A unitary Fourier/alias identity gives the exact normalized fiber frame bound. Vandermonde node equality is equivalent to the countable chord-length time resonance set. At each positive time collision phases are finite, proving injectivity. The Fourier-transformed inverse polynomial evaluation matrix gives the exact binomial small-time constant uniformly in fibers. Nonexistence of triple collisions and Lagrange inverse estimates yield two-sided quadratic resonance deterioration, with a separate exact q=2 determinant expansion. The package includes and passed a 197-check independent-numerical-implementation script, which is not treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: General fiber/Vandermonde frame criteria are fully credited to arXiv:1912.10348 and arXiv:2506.16195. The assessed specific novelty is the explicit arithmetic resonance spectrum of the one-sided shift-Poisson semigroup for every q, its injectivity at all resonances despite failure of a lower frame bound, the sharp binomial small-time constant, and the quadratic resonance collapse with the exact two-channel coefficient. Actual scientific comparisons of the cited full texts and database hit summaries did not reveal a covering proposition, although an unindexed specialization is a residual risk.
residual_risks: The algebraic method is a specialization of known dynamical-sampling fiber criteria; older unindexed papers might have already evaluated this exact directional Poisson flow or its stability asymptotics.

value.rationale: Critical-density space-time sampling is a motivated frame-inversion problem. The exact arithmetic forbidden set distinguishes injectivity from uniform stable invertibility, and the sharp all-q small-time coefficient plus resonance quadratic degeneration quantitatively describe conditioning of the natural q-channel sampling design. These specific all-scale laws go beyond the standard abstract determinant criterion.
